metadata.title: Uniform integral annihilators and potential connecting maps in a Huneke-Wiegand family
metadata.description:
We study an explicit integral connecting presentation arising in the lower Koszul strand of a previously constructed Huneke-Wiegand counterexample family. For every integer p>=8, we construct a labelled original-domain source V_p with complete boundary M_p V_p=2 eta_p, where eta_p is a fixed four-row endpoint representative. The tracked class, and its previously derived connecting representative, therefore have order dividing two and vanish after base change to any coefficient ring in which 2 is invertible.

The proof uses signed potential cycles, reflection-symmetric interval potentials, an exact triangle telescoping identity, and two original kernel-domain corrections. No omitted boundary coordinate, projected matrix, Hermite normal form, or extrapolation from finite ranks is used for the uniform annihilator. Independently, we give a complete integral potential basis for the D-kernel in one fixed-high sector, of rank binomial(p-1,2), with each basis image supported on at most seven K rows.

The record includes the independently certified failure of a radius-two source search at p=8, 861 exact potential-basis checks, and an independently reconstructed 18-parameter campaign through p=100 for the annihilator. Every full labelled source is preserved in a deterministic compressed certificate archive. The signed derivations, rather than these finite ranges, establish the uniform statements.

Scope: order dividing two is not order exactly two. Uniform nonvanishing in characteristic two, a second independent class, the full connecting quotient and its recurrence remain open. The paper does not claim to resolve the remaining Huneke-Wiegand extensions or the Jacobian conjecture. Son Pham retains priority for the original public counterexample; this is a separate homological companion to the CAOS family record. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
